Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1 (DM1) is a complex multisystemic genetic disorder caused by CTG repeat expansions in the DMPK gene, leading to RNA toxicity and widespread splicing defects. These splicing abnormalities affect multiple systems, including the respiratory, skeletal, cardiac, nervous, and endocrine systems, resulting in aggressive symptoms that significantly impact quality of life and survival. Cardiac complications are the second leading cause of deaths in DM1, after respiratory insufficiency. Current research is largely focused on understanding cardiac pathology in DM1.
